groups.observation: A large near-circular disk with a dark continuous outer rim, center near x1180,y307, spans approximately x1046..1316,y174..445. Its interior has many horizontal black hatch strokes.

Twelve dark inward-facing triangular rim markers are visible around the circumference, at top, bottom, left, right and intermediate sectors. They are scale markers, not independently readable ray arrowheads.

Short radial minor marks occur between the triangular markers. No numerical degree labels are readable on the rim. The lamp joins/obscures part of the lower-left rim; the exact complete count of minor marks is not certified.
groups.limit: Do not invent a numbered degree scale or a complete minor-tick count.

groups.observation: A smaller lower semicircular profile is inside the disk, with a nearly horizontal upper flat edge at y305 and a curved bottom near y368. Its middle is close to the disk center; the lower interior has short oblique hatch strokes.

Two dark loop-like/end features with light centers sit near the left and right ends of the smaller flat edge, approximately x1125 and x1235,y307. They descend a short distance alongside the smaller semicircle. Their physical roles are not inferred.

A tilted tube-like source is lower left of the disk and points diagonally upward/right toward the disk. It has a dark rear end, short hatch/ladder-like strokes along the tube, and an oval rim/front near x1055,y425. Several small light-centered fittings are visible at that front.
A narrow dark vertical support descends from the disk's bottom near x1172,y443 to about y569; its inner light strip is visible. No separate broad base is visible.

No alphabetic point label, alpha/beta/gamma label or numeric tick label can be independently read inside the apparatus. The printed figure number is the separate caption, not an embedded apparatus label.

Light gaps/diagonal strokes cross the dense horizontal/oblique hatching near the smaller semicircle and central flat boundary, but individual incident/reflected/refracted paths, their exact meeting points, and their direction arrowheads cannot be separated reliably. The authorized crop does not resolve this.

groups.observation: A solid horizontal line approaches the central junction from the left, around x840..1078,y1673. The lower semicircle's flat diameter lies on this line; the junction is at the midpoint of the semicircle's diameter.
A continuous lower semicircular curved boundary runs from about x889,y1673 down through x1078,y1862 and up to x1266,y1676. No grid, hatched fill or printed medium name occurs within it.
A solid vertical normal passes through the central junction, extending upward to about y1571 and downward to about y1809. It continues below both small lower angle arcs.

A solid oblique line runs from lower left, approximately x871,y1796, through the lower-left curved boundary to the central junction, direction toward upper right. No distinct arrowhead on this incoming line can be certified from the source page; do not require a newly added one.
A solid line leaves the central junction toward lower right, crosses the lower-right curved boundary and extends to about x1310,y1825. A visible arrowhead points down/right along this outgoing line.

A broken/dashed horizontal line starts at the central junction and runs rightward along the interface level, ending in a right-pointing arrow near x1323,y1677. Preserve the solid-left/broken-right distinction.

A quarter-circle-like angle arc is above/right of the junction, between the upward normal and the horizontal outgoing dashed line. The readable label is β=90. A separate degree glyph is not distinguishable; do not invent one as a faithful transcription requirement.

Two adjacent small lower angle arcs meet the downward normal: one between the incoming lower-left line and downward normal, and one between the normal and outgoing lower-right line. They must not be replaced by one undifferentiated angle.
The lower-left angle is labelled α with a small subscript 0 (α₀); the lower-right angle is labelled γ. Both sit inside the lower semicircle near their respective arcs.

All three ray-like lines and the normal meet at the same central point on the diameter. Both oblique lines cross the curved semicircular boundary; the outgoing dashed line follows the flat interface to the right. No extra labelled point or ray is discernible.

figure157.source_detail_limit: The visible paths, solid/dashed distinction, two lower angles and three labels are independently readable. Absence of a distinct incoming arrowhead or degree glyph is a source limitation, not a licensed modern addition.
